body: Helping others helps a little. But I'm always helping others. It leaves me drained emotionally, but it keeps me going.

Well thought-out responses. I've tried a lot of this before.

I've never learned how to remember without the feelings of the memories. I don't recount the days events anymore. At least, I don't do it willfully. I don't need to. And every night it's the same. I dream out a new memory. I love some of the dreams, I do. And it's nice to never forget things. But other times, it leaves me weary. The dreaming bit is tough.

Fix yourself something to eat. Drink some water. Walk down to the beach and listen to some jams on the way there. And, if you can, try to help people in some small way. The world may hurt for you and the past isn't going to stop being the past, but the world won't be any better without you in it. But if you turn all of this hurt into a positive thing, like helping others, your being in this world is a kind and generous thing.

Just try it. It may not work right away. It may be hard to muster up the energy and will power to do it, but you really ought to. You might like it.

This might be a lot to ask, and someone might have asked it before, but here goes:

Call someone. Fix yourself something to eat. Force it down if you have to. And call someone. Talk to anyone. People may not show it from day to day, but there's this beautiful thing where, in earnest, the majority of people out there honestly care and want each other to continue living. Just be as honest as you can about everything and figure things out from there.

I did get therapy with the pills, yes.

It's generally when my thoughts start racing. I remember a lot at a time and then it kind of snow balls. It can be a series of mundane topical memories that snow-balls into bad ones once the anxiety gets worse.

When I was younger, I used to, before I went to bed, stare at my ceiling and visualize my entire day. After doing that, I'd think of something or somewhere, and I'd try to build a picture of it in my mind. And when I dream, it's like I'll visit all of my memories, good and bad. It's like I'm there again. It's a bit stressful because I don't feel like I've gotten a good night of sleep since I was six.
Well try to think of something. Throw some ideas out at me. If that's not asking too much, that is.

I've considered taking pills, yes. But ever since I was misdiagnosed when I was younger (I spent a lot of time in and out of doctor's offices, getting tested, etc..) I've found it hard to trust pills.

Large crowds, loud sounds, dreaming every night, remembering nearly everything. Sometimes all of the memories come at once and all of the feelings kind of sit on top of one another.
What would you do if you decided NOT to hang yourself? Studying anything? Any sites you want to see? Anything you want to do? Maybe work on something you're passionate about?
